Architecture and design decisions

Application layers

  • news.models owns the normalised domain data and validation.

  • news.forms validates browser input and role-filtered membership choices.

  • news.policies scopes visibility, editing and subscription querysets.

  • news.views handles authenticated HTML workflows.

  • news.api and news.serializers expose authenticated JSON endpoints.

  • news.services coordinates approval, email and integration delivery.

  • news.signals synchronises role groups and constrains subscriptions.

Transactions and delivery

Approval locks the article row in an atomic transaction. Delivery is scheduled with transaction.on_commit so the callback observes committed approval. Email and API completion are recorded separately. This is synchronous delivery, not a durable job queue. A partial email failure may repeat some recipients on retry. A production design would use an outbox/worker and stronger idempotency.

The container runs Gunicorn with two workers and four threads each. Threads allow the approval callback to be handled while the originating request waits for it. The callback URL uses the container’s own loopback address and port. The callback checks authentication, approval and editor permission.

Role-aware data

Users select Reader, Editor or Journalist. Reader subscriptions, independent articles and independent newsletters are exposed through role-aware properties that return None when inapplicable. Many-to-many membership tables preserve normalisation rather than duplicating role-specific fields.

Repository history

The initial commit imports the final capstone. The docs branch documents models, policies and services in separate commits, then adds Sphinx sources and built HTML. The container branch starts separately from the initial main branch and adds Docker configuration. Both are merged into main, followed by the setup README. Generated caches and secrets are ignored; documentation HTML is the intentional exception requested by the brief.
